newsitem.title: USA: J&L expects capital expenses to increase.
newsitem.headline: J&L expects capital expenses to increase.

text.p: J&L Specialty Steel Inc said Wednesday construction of the Direct Roll Anneal & Pickle Line at its Midland, Pa., plant should be completed in December.
Commissioning should begin in the first half of 1997, and full production is expected in the second half, the company said. Investment in the new line is expected to be about $95 million in 1996.
Total capital expenditures for J&L's five year capital plan are expected to increase 10 to 15 percent from an originally estimated $200 million, the company said.
The increase is mainly because of additional spending for the Direct Roll Anneal & Pickle line, the company said.
The DRAP line is meant to be a single continuous processing line for stainless steel, which J&L said has not been tried before.

The company said that after construction began it became clear that the project was "more complex and more costly than originally anticipated, and that the line's operating capabilities by making certain scope changes."

The DRAP line is longer than four football fields. J&L said it will increase its finishing capacity by 80 percent and process about 275,000 tons a year. It should reduce processing time by as much as 75 percent, the company said.
J&L began its five-year plan in 1993. The company said total capital expenditures for 1996 and 1997 should remain about $150 million because it has deferred plans to expand its melt shop.
